threads.subject: TMS export: CO2 per shipment column from week 44

emails.body:
We want to show CO2 per shipment on the logistics KPI dashboard and would like to get it straight from the TMS export instead of calculating it in Excel.

Could you add a column co2_kg_per_shipment to the standard shipment export? Our scope:
- road legs only, no sea or rail
- well-to-wheel (WTW), calculated according to the GLEC framework
- value in kg, per shipment

Pieter Bakker (in cc) maintains the dashboard mapping and needs a sample file before he can change anything. Our target is that the column is in the export from week 44. Is that realistic on your side?

Thanks Tom, this is feasible. We can enable the column co2_kg_per_shipment for your tenant so that it appears in the export from week 44 (Monday 26 October).

Points to be aware of:
- The calculation covers road legs only, WTW, based on GLEC default emission factors per vehicle type and distance.
- As long as carriers do not send actual fuel consumption, the value is an estimate based on these defaults.
- Decimal separator is a dot, two decimals, empty value for shipments without a road leg.

I attached a sample export with 5 shipments so Pieter can start on the mapping.

Got the sample, thanks. The file loads fine, I only need to add the new field to the mapping in the dashboard data model. Two questions before I do:

1. Row 80412377 (Felixstowe - Rotterdam) has an empty CO2 value. I assume that is the sea leg, so it is correctly left out? I will show it as blank, not as 0, otherwise the monthly average gets distorted.
2. Should the dashboard show the number as a fact or as an estimate? Since carriers do not deliver actual fuel data yet, I would rather label it.

1. Yes, Felixstowe - Rotterdam is a sea shipment, so no road leg and no value. Blank is right, please exclude blanks from the average.
2. Agree, label it. Please call the tile "CO2 (est.)" with a tooltip that says: road legs only, WTW, GLEC, estimate until carriers deliver actual fuel data. I do not have a date for the actual data from the carriers yet, so I would not promise anything in the tooltip.

Can you have the updated mapping ready in the test dashboard by Wednesday? Then I can compare a few shipments against my own calculation before the first real export.

The mapping is updated in the test dashboard. co2_kg_per_shipment is now loaded as a numeric field, blanks are excluded from the average, and the tile is labelled "CO2 (est.)" with the tooltip you described.

I loaded the 5 sample rows. Total for the 4 road shipments is 724.25 kg, average 181.06 kg per shipment. Mark, I added you in cc because the tile will appear on the management view as well. The production dashboard switches to the new field with the first export of week 44; until then the tile stays empty.
Thanks Pieter, will check the test dashboard this morning.

facts.text: From week 44 (Monday 26 October 2026) the TMS shipment export contains a column co2_kg_per_shipment.
The CO2 value covers road legs only; sea and rail are not included.
The calculation is well-to-wheel (WTW) and follows the GLEC framework.
Tom de Vries's colleague Tom Hendriks requested the column from RouteWise; Pieter Bakker maintains the dashboard mapping.
RouteWise calculates the value with GLEC default emission factors per vehicle type and distance, so it is an estimate until carriers send actual fuel consumption.
The export uses a dot as decimal separator, two decimals, and an empty value for shipments without a road leg.
RouteWise supplied a sample export with 5 shipments (sample_export_co2_wk44.xlsx) for Pieter to build the mapping.
Delivery 80412377 (Felixstowe - Rotterdam) is a sea shipment and has a blank CO2 value.
Blank CO2 values are shown as blank instead of 0 and excluded from the average, to avoid distorting the monthly average.
The dashboard tile is labelled "CO2 (est.)" with a tooltip: road legs only, WTW, GLEC, estimate until carriers deliver actual fuel data.
There is no date yet for when carriers will deliver actual fuel data.
On 21 October Pieter updated the mapping in the test dashboard; the production dashboard switches to the new field with the first export of week 44.
In the sample, the 4 road shipments total 724.25 kg CO2, an average of 181.06 kg per shipment; Hamburg - Venlo (482 km) is 431.75 kg.
Mark de Boer was put in cc because the tile will also appear on the management view.

questions.q: From when does the TMS export contain the co2_kg_per_shipment column?
Why is the CO2 figure on the dashboard labelled as an estimate?
questions.a: Because it is based on GLEC default emission factors; carriers have not yet delivered actual fuel consumption data.

questions.q: Which transport legs are included in the CO2 per shipment value?
questions.a: Road legs only, calculated well-to-wheel according to the GLEC framework.

questions.q: Who updated the dashboard mapping for the new CO2 column?
How are shipments without a road leg, such as Felixstowe - Rotterdam delivery 80412377, treated in the dashboard average?
questions.a: Their CO2 value is blank, shown as blank (not 0) and excluded from the average.

questions.q: When will carriers deliver the actual fuel data for the CO2 calculation?
